paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. God's plan doesn't hinge on how the work feels in the moment. The Servant says, "I have labored in vain," and in the very next breath He says, "yet My vindication is with the LORD, and My reward is with My God" (Isaiah 49:4). When you're worn out and the results look blurry, your reward isn't sitting in how the batch turned out. It's sitting with God.

And then God goes bigger than anybody asked. Raising up the tribes of Jacob wasn't enough, so the LORD says, "I will also make You a light for the nations, to bring My salvation to the ends of the earth" (Isaiah 49:6). The Servant was despised and abhorred by the nation, and still kings will see Him and rise (Isaiah 49:7). I can't STAMP my way to that kind of plan, baker, but God doesn't need me to. His plan is bigger than any one of us can see.

So what does that mean for you? God makes room for people far away, for prisoners, for those in darkness, and He leads them "beside springs of water" (Isaiah 49:10). The One who has compassion on them is the One doing the guiding, and that's why heaven and earth get to sing. If you've ever felt overlooked, keep going with a glad heart, because the LORD "has comforted His people" (Isaiah 49:13).
